correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the generating product exactly. The overpartition theta identity forces P=1+2B and B modulo two is the positive-square indicator; squaring gives 4(B+B²) modulo eight and the Frobenius square has even-degree support. Euler pentagonal then identifies odd-index coefficients with four times an exactly defined pentagonal-plus-square count. The bijection (j,s)->(6j−1,2s) is one-to-four on all signed \(x^2+3y^2\) representations for \(N=12n+1\equiv13\pmod{24}\), with no zero-coordinate exceptions. For odd N the Eisenstein-ring ideal factorization gives \(r_3(N)=2H(N)\), correctly normalized by two representatives per norm ideal. Thus the infinite congruence is proved, not extrapolated from computation. H(N) parity and the 4-residue criterion follow from complete prime-power factorization. Density-one follows from independent exact-exponent-one events over finite split-prime sets, divergence of their sum, and a monotone finite-sieve bound; infinitely many 4-residue indices follow from primes 13 mod24. Exact independent modular partition recurrence, norm enumeration and divisor enumeration checked 600 odd indices to 1200; these are not used as infinite proofs.

evidence: The published modulus-seven congruence for a4 cannot imply a classification modulo eight since seven and eight are coprime and the progression covers only one modulo-seven class.
A framework stated only for modulo-three progressions does not by itself imply the modulo-eight law.
The 1998 quadratic representation formula gives r3(N), but lacks the required modulo-eight reduction of the partition series; the character sum alone cannot imply \(a_4(n)\) residues.
A published record on modulo-four parity of singular overpartitions concerns different generating functions and does not subsume this claim.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact claim is an identity between the four-colored partition coefficients on every positive odd index and a Dirichlet-character divisor sum, with a complete prime-factor residue classification. The inspected primary results do not give that connection or its density conclusion.

evidence: OEIS A002324 indexes the divisor difference with prime-power factors, not its equality modulo eight to odd coefficients of F4.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant 2025 primary full text defines exactly the same colored-partition sequence but proves a modulo-seven congruence, not the complete odd-index modulo-eight coefficient-divisor formula. The September 2026 abstract concerns a modulo-three framework; full text could not be inspected and is a residual risk. The classical \(x^2+3y^2\) representation formula and the OEIS character sum are correctly treated as established ingredients, not claimed original. Published-record searches using exact products, formulas, aliases and quadratic representations did not identify a stronger covering claim; these search failures are not treated as a proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The full September 2026 paper could not be accessed; although its abstract specifically treats congruences modulo three, a relevant appendix or aside cannot be ruled out.
An unindexed differently named theorem about the same eta quotient may imply the stated odd-index law. An independent literature review remains needed.

value.rationale: The coefficient-divisor identity gives an exact complete arithmetic classification at every odd index of a recent natural partition family, rather than a single prescribed progression. Its unusual quadratic-norm conversion yields concrete prime-factor congruence tests, including exact identification of exceptional four residues. It proves a density-one modulo-eight property while retaining infinitely many explicitly parameterized exceptions. These results settle a motivated 2-adic classification question for a whole parity component; no paper-scale generalization or artificial cutoff is required.
